Hi Paulina,

At this point I'd not suggest that anyone submit a license without using a
lawyer.

We discourage submissions of "badgeware" terms - those requiring a display
of the software vendor's information - mainly because of the combinatorial
problem. Badgeware doesn't look harmful when one company does it, but when
50 do, and software is combined as is usual with Open Source, it becomes an
unreasonable burden on the user.

In addition, the implementation of the badgeware term as an *invariant
section* of the software - one with modification prohibited - would prevent
the license from being considered Open Source.

I think it's actually difficult to enforce a performance requirement - the
registration requirement - in a copyright license rather than a
conventional contract where both parties have indicated their assent. At
least in the U.S. This is something a lawyer could tell you. And in any
case that sort of term has not been accepted for OSI-approved Open Source
licenses.
